indicators.scientific_definition: Mean occupied-neighbour same-group fraction across agents at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Local similarity is the individual exposure primitive; its cross-agent mean captures average local segmentation pressure.

indicators.semantic_name: Standard deviation of local same-group similarity
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-agent dispersion of occupied-neighbour same-group fraction at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Dispersion of local similarity measures individual heterogeneity in local group exposure.

indicators.scientific_definition: Mean occupied Moore-neighbour count across agents at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Mean neighbour count reflects local occupancy density experienced by individual agents.

indicators.scientific_definition: Proportion of agents whose local same-group fraction is below tolerance at each step, computed as the boolean dissatisfaction event fraction over agents.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher tolerance raises the minimum required same-group fraction, so more agents are classified as unsatisfied.

indicators.scientific_rationale: The unsatisfied fraction is the aggregate prevalence of the elementary dissatisfaction event.

indicators.semantic_name: Mean local similarity among unsatisfied agents
indicators.scientific_definition: Mean local same-group fraction among agents classified as unsatisfied at each step, excluding satisfied agents by boolean masking.
indicators.scientific_rationale: This observable describes the typical local context of agents currently trying to relocate.

indicators.scientific_definition: Proportion of agents that relocated during each recorded step, computed as the boolean relocation event fraction over agents.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher move_probability increases the chance an unsatisfied agent attempts relocation, raising the fraction that moves.

indicators.scientific_rationale: The moving fraction is the aggregate prevalence of the elementary relocation event.

indicators.scientific_definition: Mean periodic Manhattan distance of relocation among agents that moved during each step, excluding non-movers.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Mean move distance captures the spatial extent of individual relocation events.

indicators.scientific_definition: Mean same-group neighbour fraction at selected destinations among agents that relocated during each step, excluding non-movers.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher destination_preference increases the probability of selecting the most similar sampled vacancy, raising average destination similarity among movers.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Destination similarity measures the local exposure outcome of relocation choices.

indicators.scientific_definition: Proportion of agents with at least one occupied different-group neighbour at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Boundary exposure indicates how many individuals are directly adjacent to out-group members.

indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-agent standard deviation of destination same-group neighbour fraction, including zero for non-movers, at each step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Dispersion of destination similarity reflects heterogeneity in relocation outcomes.

indicators.scientific_definition: Lower quartile of agents' local same-group fraction at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Lower quartile tracks the most isolated fraction of individuals.

indicators.scientific_definition: Upper quartile of agents' local same-group fraction at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Upper quartile tracks the most grouped fraction of individuals.

indicators.scientific_definition: Shannon entropy of binned local same-group similarity across agents at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Entropy summarizes the diversity of local exposure states in the agent population.

indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-agent standard deviation of periodic Manhattan relocation distance, including zero for non-movers, at each step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Dispersion of move distance captures variability in relocation spatial reach.

indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-agent standard deviation of occupied Moore-neighbour count at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Dispersion of neighbour count reflects unevenness in local occupancy density.

indicators.scientific_definition: Ratio of moving agents to unsatisfied agents at each step, measuring the realized relocation response among dissatisfied agents.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher move_probability increases the chance that an unsatisfied agent attempts relocation, raising the ratio of movers to unsatisfied agents.

indicators.scientific_rationale: This interaction-level observable links the dissatisfaction event to the relocation event.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of mean local similarity
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of district-averaged local same-group similarity at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Uses fixed district membership to aggregate local similarity within districts and capture between-district segregation variation.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of unsatisfied fraction
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of district-level unsatisfied-agent fraction at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district variation in dissatisfaction reveals uneven local stability pressure across public spatial districts.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of boundary-agent fraction
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of the district-level proportion of agents with at least one different-group neighbour at each step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: District-level boundary exposure variation captures local intergroup contact differences across fixed public domains.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of moving fraction
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of the district-level proportion of agents that relocated during each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district variation in relocation activity indicates uneven local adjustment pressure.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of destination similarity
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of district-averaged destination same-group neighbour fraction at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district dispersion of destination similarity captures local differences in relocation destination quality.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of mean neighbour count
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of district-averaged occupied Moore-neighbour count at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district variation in local occupancy density identifies uneven packing across fixed spatial domains.

indicators.scientific_definition: Average district-level entropy of agent group labels within each fixed public district at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Mean district composition entropy measures within-district group mixing while using supplied district membership structure.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district standard deviation of mean move distance
indicators.scientific_definition: Cross-district dispersion of district-averaged periodic Manhattan relocation distance at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district variation in move distance captures distinct local spatial mobility patterns.

indicators.scientific_definition: Whole-system proportion of unsatisfied agents computed from the system aggregate unsatisfied count at each recorded step.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher tolerance increases the global number of unsatisfied agents, raising the whole-system unsatisfied fraction.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Whole-system dissatisfaction is a core collective outcome of the segregation process.

indicators.scientific_definition: Whole-system proportion of agents that relocated during each recorded step, computed as the ratio of relocation-event count to agent population.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher move_probability increases the global relocation frequency, raising the whole-system moving fraction.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Global relocation fraction is a whole-system measure of aggregate adjustment intensity.

indicators.scientific_definition: Number of contiguous occupied-cell components with identical group label in the periodic grid at each recorded step, excluding vacancies.
indicators.scientific_rationale: The number of same-group contiguous components is a global structural measure of spatial sorting.

indicators.scientific_definition: Whole-grid average same-group similarity among occupied Moore neighbours at each recorded step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Global spatial neighbour similarity is a direct whole-grid metric of segregation.

interpretation_boundary: Indicators are declarative, executable observables computed from the supplied raw fields and grammar. They do not provide statistical estimates, causal effects, temporal forecasts, or intervention contrasts; no candidate paths or predictions are asserted in this phase.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher tolerance increases the fraction of unsatisfied agents, which amplifies between-district differences in relocation activity and thereby raises the whole-system moved fraction.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: More unsatisfied agents attempt relocation, increasing district-level dispersion of moving fractions, and this dispersed local activation raises the global relocation fraction.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Observed meso_district_move_fraction_std or macro_global_moved_fraction does not increase under tolerance plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher tolerance increases dissatisfaction, causing agents to move away from mixed-group boundaries; this reduces between-district boundary-fraction dispersion while strengthening whole-grid same-group neighbour similarity.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Stronger homophilic relocation removes boundary contacts and produces more homogeneous spatial sorting, lowering district boundary variation and raising global spatial similarity.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global spatial neighbour similarity does not increase under tolerance plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher tolerance intensifies segregation pressure, reducing district group-composition entropy and consolidating same-group areas into fewer contiguous components.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: As dissatisfaction rises, agents sort into more homogeneous districts, lowering group entropy and merging adjacent same-group clusters, which decreases the global connected-component count.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global connected components does not decrease under tolerance plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Lower tolerance reduces the share of unsatisfied agents and district-level variation in dissatisfaction, while weaker sorting pressure allows spatial clusters to fragment into more same-group components.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Fewer agents are classified as unsatisfied, so between-district dissatisfaction dispersion falls, and less homophilic relocation prevents large cluster consolidation, increasing the number of same-group components.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global connected components does not increase under tolerance minus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Lower tolerance reduces relocation pressure, lowering district-level moving-fraction dispersion and whole-grid spatial neighbour similarity as more mixed neighbourhoods persist.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: With fewer unsatisfied agents, relocation activity declines and becomes less spatially variable, weakening homophilic sorting and reducing global same-group adjacency.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global spatial neighbour similarity does not decrease under tolerance minus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher tolerance raises dissatisfaction, leading to more variable destination-similarity outcomes across districts while consolidating same-group areas into fewer connected components.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Stronger homophilic relocation increases between-district dispersion of destination similarity and merges adjacent same-group clusters, thereby decreasing the global component count.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global connected components does not decrease under tolerance plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher move probability increases the realized relocation response among unsatisfied agents, amplifies cross-district dispersion in moving rates, and raises the global relocation fraction.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: More dissatisfied agents act on their dissatisfaction, creating greater district-level variability in movement and increasing whole-system relocation activity.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global moved fraction does not increase under move_probability plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher move probability increases relocation frequency, producing more variable destination-similarity outcomes across districts and raising global spatial neighbour similarity through repeated homophilic sorting.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: More moves allow more agents to enter high-similarity destinations, increasing district-level destination-similarity dispersion and whole-grid same-group adjacency.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global spatial neighbour similarity does not increase under move_probability plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Lower move probability weakens the relocation response of unsatisfied agents, increasing between-district dissatisfaction dispersion and raising the whole-system unsatisfied fraction because fewer agents escape poor local conditions.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: When unsatisfied agents are less likely to move, dissatisfaction persists unevenly across districts and globally, leading to higher global unsatisfied fraction.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global unhappy fraction does not increase under move_probability minus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Lower move probability reduces relocation frequency, allowing boundary contacts to persist unevenly across districts and preventing same-group cluster consolidation, which increases the number of spatial components.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Less movement preserves heterogeneous boundary patterns and spatial fragmentation, raising district boundary-fraction dispersion and global connected-component count.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global connected components does not increase under move_probability minus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher move probability increases relocation frequency, producing greater between-district variation in local neighbour counts, but more movement resolves dissatisfaction and lowers the global unsatisfied fraction.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Relocation disperses agents and alters local occupancy, increasing district neighbour-count dispersion while moving more unsatisfied agents to acceptable neighbourhoods, thereby reducing global dissatisfaction.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global unhappy fraction does not decrease under move_probability plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher destination preference makes movers select more similar destinations, increasing average destination similarity and district-level destination-similarity dispersion, and raising whole-grid spatial neighbour similarity.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Selective relocation concentrates agents in high-similarity locations, increasing cross-district variation in destination quality and strengthening global segregation.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global spatial neighbour similarity does not increase under destination_preference plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher destination preference moves agents away from mixed boundaries, reducing boundary-fraction dispersion and lowering global dissatisfaction as more agents reach satisfying neighbourhoods.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Stronger preference for similar destinations removes agents from boundary contact and reduces the share of unsatisfied agents system-wide.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global unhappy fraction does not decrease under destination_preference plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Higher destination preference increases destination similarity, reduces district group-composition entropy, and consolidates same-group areas into fewer connected components.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Preferential homophilic moves create more homogeneous districts and merge adjacent same-group clusters, lowering both district entropy and global component count.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global connected components does not decrease under destination_preference plus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Lower destination preference reduces average destination similarity and district-level destination-similarity dispersion, but less selective sorting leaves more agents unsatisfied globally.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Weaker preference lowers destination quality and spatial differentiation while preventing dissatisfied agents from reaching satisfying neighbourhoods, raising global dissatisfaction.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global unhappy fraction does not increase under destination_preference minus.

candidate_paths.scientific_rationale: Lower destination preference produces less directed moves, increasing district-level dispersion of relocation distances and fragmenting spatial clusters, which raises the count of connected components.
candidate_paths.mechanistic_explanation: Random destination choices lead to longer, more variable relocation distances and prevent same-group cluster consolidation, increasing the global component count.
candidate_paths.falsification_condition: Macro global connected components does not increase under destination_preference minus.
